title: Homophones
learning_objectives: use context clues to choose the correct homophone

sequence.script: Hi there! I am Bloom, and I am so excited to learn with you today! Today we are going to explore something really cool about words. Some words sound exactly the same when you say them out loud, but they mean completely different things and are spelled differently. These special words are called homophones!

Let me say that again. Homophones are words that sound the same but have different meanings and different spellings. The word homophone comes from Greek. Homo means same, and phone means sound. Same sound!

Here is our first example. Sea and see. Say them out loud. Sea and see. They sound identical! But sea is the big body of water where fish live and waves crash. And see means to look at something with your eyes. Same sound, totally different meanings!

Here is another one. Bear and bare. A bear is the big furry animal that lives in the forest. But bare means empty or uncovered, like bare feet with no shoes! Bear and bare. Same sound, different meanings.

One more example before we practice. Knight and night. A knight is a brave warrior in shining armor from long ago. And night is the dark time when the stars come out and we go to sleep. Knight and night!
Now it is your turn! Can you think of a pair of homophones? Any pair you know!

interaction.fallback_script: That is okay! One example is write and right. Write means to put words on paper, and right means correct or a direction.

sequence.script: Great work! Now let us practice. Listen to this sentence. I went to the blank to swim. Is the missing word A, sea, or B, see?

interaction.correct_response_script: Yes! A, sea, is correct! You go to the sea to swim. Sea is the big body of water. Fantastic job!
interaction.incorrect_response_script: Not quite! The answer is A, sea. Sea is the big body of water where you swim. See means to look at something.
interaction.fallback_script: The answer is A, sea! Sea is the big body of water where you go to swim.

sequence.script: Here is another one. The blank growled and looked for honey in the forest. Is the missing word A, bear, or B, bare?

interaction.correct_response_script: That is right! A, bear, is correct! A bear is the furry animal that loves honey. You are doing amazing!
interaction.incorrect_response_script: Good try! The answer is A, bear. A bear is the big furry animal that growls and looks for honey.
interaction.fallback_script: The answer is A, bear! A bear is the furry animal that lives in the forest and loves honey.

sequence.script: Last practice question! I want to blank a story in my journal. Is the missing word A, write, or B, right?

interaction.correct_response_script: Excellent! A, write, is correct! Write means to put words on paper, exactly what you do in a journal. You are a homophone superstar!
interaction.incorrect_response_script: Almost! The answer is A, write. Write means to put words on paper or in a journal. Right means correct or a direction.
interaction.fallback_script: The answer is A, write! Write means to put words on paper, like writing in a journal.

sequence.script: You did such a great job today! Let us review what we learned. Homophones are words that sound the same but have different meanings and spellings. We practiced sea and see, bear and bare, knight and night, and write and right. The trick is to always think about what the sentence means to pick the right one!
I am so proud of how hard you worked today! Keep your ears open for homophones out in the world. You might be surprised how many you find. See you next time!
